nodes.instructions:
Implement app_server/__init__.py create_app() per the Foundation Contract, app_server/testing.py web_client(), a base HTML template with minimal CSS, and a GET /health route returning 200.

The factory opens the database through open_database using the configured DSN and registers blueprints from later stories; it invents no other routes.

nodes.summary: Add a book with a title and author and persist it.
nodes.instructions:
Implement a book service add function and POST /books accepting JSON with title and author. A valid submission returns 201 with the stored book (id, title, author) and persists it via books.create.

Write pytest tests under tests/ covering the add behavior, including a round trip read-back.
nodes.name: Add a book with a title and author and persist it.

nodes.summary: List books in the order they were added.
nodes.instructions:
Implement GET /books returning 200 with a JSON array of books ordered by insertion (id ascending) via books.list. An empty list returns an empty array.

Write pytest tests adding several books and asserting the returned order equals the order submitted.
nodes.name: List books in the order they were added.

nodes.summary: Remove a book so it no longer appears in the list.
nodes.instructions:
Implement DELETE /books/{book_id}: 204 when the book existed and is deleted, 404 for an unknown id. A removed book must never reappear in later reads.

Write pytest tests for removal, absence on the next list read, preserved order of remaining books, and the unknown-id 404.
nodes.name: Remove a book so it no longer appears in the list.

nodes.summary: Reject a submission with an empty title or author with a clear error.
nodes.instructions:
Add validation in the service layer used by POST /books. A missing, empty, or whitespace-only title or author is rejected with status 400 and a JSON body carrying a clear human-readable error naming the offending field. Nothing is stored on rejection.

Write pytest tests for empty title, empty author, both empty, and whitespace-only values, asserting status and that the list is unchanged.
nodes.name: Reject a submission with an empty title or author with a clear error.

nodes.summary: Render the reading list page with an add form, error display, and remove buttons.
nodes.instructions:
GET / renders books in the order added with a title and author add form and a remove button per book. POST /add processes the form through the book service: success redirects (303) to /; empty title or author re-renders the page with status 400 and a visible error message. POST /remove/{book_id} removes the book and redirects (303) to /.

acceptance.intent: GET / answers 200 and shows an added book's title and author, and GET /books agrees with it on the same book.
POST /add with a title and author redirects 303 and the book then appears on GET / and in GET /books.
POST /add with an empty title, an empty author, or whitespace-only values answers 400 and stores nothing.
POST /remove/{book_id} redirects 303 and the book is gone from GET / and GET /books; an unknown id also redirects 303.
GET / presents books in the order they were added.

nodes.summary: Provide bin/test.sh and prove the complete suite passes end to end.
nodes.instructions:
Create a POSIX sh bin/test.sh runnable as sh bin/test.sh from the application root. It activates .venv when present, runs pytest -q, and exits with pytest's exit status, zero only when every test passes.

Run sh bin/test.sh and sh sources/full_test.sh and preserve command, exit code, stdout, and stderr as evidence. Confirm tests exist for add, ordered listing, removal, and empty title or author rejection.

The pytest runner is installed and starts from the application root.
books.create stores a book and returns the declared Output row carrying the supplied title and author.
books.get reads back a created book by id with the stored title and author.
books.list returns books in the order they were added.
books.delete removes a book so it no longer appears in the next list read, and leaves other books in place.
create_app returns a Flask application.
web_client returns a usable test client for a testing-mode app.
GET /health is reachable and answers 200 with a JSON body.
A path no feature declares is absent and answers 404.
POST /books answers 201 and returns the title and author that were supplied, with an id.
A submitted book is read back from the store with the supplied title and author.
Two books added in sequence receive ascending ids, preserving insertion order.
GET /books returns the books added during the check in the order they were added.
Each listed book carries the supplied title and author and its id.
GET /books is reachable and returns a JSON array even when no check data exists.
Removing an added book answers 204 and the book is absent from the next list read.
Removing an id that does not exist answers 404, and removing the same id twice answers 404 the second time.
Removing the middle book leaves the other books in the order they were added.
POST /books with an empty title answers 400 and stores nothing.
POST /books with an empty author answers 400 and stores nothing.
POST /books with both fields empty answers 400 and stores nothing.
Whitespace-only and missing fields are rejected with 400 and nothing is stored.
validate_book_input raises ValueError for an empty title or author.
A submission with both fields present is still accepted with 201 after validation is in place.
GET / answers 200 and shows an added book's title and author, and GET /books agrees with it on the same book.
POST /add with a title and author redirects 303 and the book then appears on GET / and in GET /books.
POST /add with an empty title, an empty author, or whitespace-only values answers 400 and stores nothing.
POST /remove/{book_id} redirects 303 and the book is gone from GET / and GET /books; an unknown id also redirects 303.
GET / presents books in the order they were added.

nodes.instructions:
Create a POSIX sh bin/test.sh runnable as sh bin/test.sh from the application root. It activates .venv when present, runs pytest -q, and exits with pytest's exit status, zero only when every test passes.

Run sh bin/test.sh and sh sources/full_test.sh and preserve command, exit code, stdout, and stderr as evidence. Confirm tests exist for add, ordered listing, removal, and empty title or author rejection.
